note: Curated type pairings. Every family is on Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License, and on Fontsource as @fontsource/<slug>. `display.weight` is the heading weight, `tracking` its letter-spacing; body text uses 400/500/600. Moods match wada.py plus technical, editorial and friendly.

pairings.name: Ledger
pairings.why: A soft, slightly wonky serif for headings over a sturdy humanist text face: trustworthy without feeling corporate.

pairings.name: Signal
pairings.why: Quirky geometric headings give character to dense, data-heavy screens that Inter keeps legible.

pairings.name: Workshop
pairings.why: Characterful headings and a friendly, open text face: a tool that feels made by people.

pairings.name: Atlas
pairings.why: An elegant condensed serif for large headlines; quiet sans text lets it carry the page.

pairings.name: Plex
pairings.why: One family with a matching mono: engineered, neutral and consistent from tables to code.

pairings.name: Masthead
pairings.why: A newsroom grotesk: confident headings and compact, readable text in one family.

pairings.name: Harbor
pairings.why: Clean, slightly rounded geometry that reads calm and modern in dashboards and settings.

pairings.name: Meadow
pairings.why: Round, approachable headings with an easy text face: consumer apps and onboarding.

pairings.name: Gazette
pairings.why: High-contrast display serif from the same design family as its sans: classic editorial with a modern body.

pairings.name: Orbit
pairings.why: Wide geometric headings feel precise and forward-looking; Inter keeps the interface dense and clear.

pairings.name: Terminal
pairings.why: Sharp, minimal and developer-native, with a mono that matches the sans exactly.

pairings.name: Quarterly
pairings.why: A reading serif made for screens with a neutral civic sans: considered and credible.

pairings.name: Premiere
pairings.why: Dramatic, high-contrast headlines for a landing page that should feel premium.

pairings.name: Foundry
pairings.why: A robust grotesk with industrial roots: strong headings, efficient body, no frills.

pairings.name: Poster
pairings.why: An expressive display face for one loud moment per page; Inter calms everything else.

pairings.name: Sprout
pairings.why: Clean and friendly with excellent small-size legibility: forms, lists and mobile screens.

pairings.name: Breeze
pairings.why: A polished contemporary sans that feels fresh in both product UI and marketing.

pairings.name: Clarity
pairings.why: Designed for reading fluency: generous widths for audiences where clarity beats density.

pairings.name: Timber
pairings.why: A sturdy slab for headings feels grounded and crafted; a humanist sans keeps text easy.

pairings.name: Almanac
pairings.why: A bookish old-style serif with a characterful grotesk: thoughtful, literary, warm.

pairings.name: Manifesto
pairings.why: Heavy, tight headlines that make a point; the same family stays readable in text.

pairings.name: Optical
pairings.classification: superfamily: display, text and mono cuts
pairings.why: Separate display and text cuts of one superfamily: optical sizes done properly, plus a matching mono.

pairings.name: Civic
pairings.why: A dependable gothic: neutral, institutional and highly legible at every size.

pairings.name: Launch
pairings.why: Wide, playful display type for a hero that should feel energetic; Manrope keeps the rest tidy.

pairings.name: Hearth
pairings.why: A chunky, warm serif adds homeliness to headings without slowing down a practical UI.

pairings.name: Salon
pairings.why: Refined Garamond headings over a humanist sans: luxury, hospitality and craft.

pairings.name: Playground
pairings.why: Slightly rounded corners make everything feel soft and playful; good for consumer and education apps.

pairings.name: Nordic
pairings.why: Restrained and even: lets colour and content lead in calm, minimal interfaces.

pairings.name: Bureau
pairings.why: A grotesk with a light humanist touch: professional but not cold.

pairings.name: Essay
pairings.why: A serif drawn for screens gives content pages a literary voice while the UI stays sans.

pairings.name: Console
pairings.why: Monospaced headings signal a developer tool at a glance; Inter keeps prose readable.

pairings.name: Loam
pairings.why: A gently calligraphic serif with a plain grotesk: natural, organic, unhurried.
